correctness.rationale: Let \(H_\gamma(x,y)=\sqrt{x^2+(1-\gamma^2)y^2}\). The six vertices of the \(N_\gamma\)-unit ball lie on the \(H_\gamma\)-unit ellipse, so convexity gives \(H_\gamma\le N_\gamma\). Weighted Cauchy gives \(|x|+(1-\gamma)|y|\le\sqrt{2/(1+\gamma)}H_\gamma\), and for \(0<\gamma<1/2\) this factor also dominates the axis branch \(|y|\). Hence \(N_\gamma\le\sqrt{2/(1+\gamma)}H_\gamma\), and Hilbert-space Ptolemy yields \(C_{\mathrm{Pt}}\le2/(1+\gamma)\). The explicit triple \(x=(-1,0)\), \(y=(\gamma,1)\), \(z=(-(1+\gamma),1)\) has the six required norms \(2,2,1,1,1,1+2\gamma\), giving ratio \(2/(1+\gamma)\). A fresh symbolic replay independently reproduced this ratio.
correctness.risk: The theorem is restricted to the stated first parameter regime; the inaccessible 2015 reconsideration paper remains a literature-access risk.

value.rationale: The Ptolemy constant is a standard quantitative inner-product defect. The family is a classical explicit hexagonal deformation, and the theorem gives the exact first nontrivial parameter regime with a sharp equality mechanism between Euclidean distortion and a concrete Ptolemy witness. This is a motivated geometric boundary calculation rather than an arbitrary numeric slice.
value.risk: The contribution is an exact regime classification for one classical planar family, not a general Ptolemy theory.

final_claim: For the real hexagonal plane with \(N_\gamma(x,y)=\max\{|y|,|x|+(1-\gamma)|y|\}\) and \(0<\gamma<1/2\), the Ptolemy constant is exactly \(C_{\mathrm{Pt}}=2/(1+\gamma)\).
limitations: Only the real two-dimensional family and \(0<\gamma<1/2\) are claimed.
